newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Amato to give up anti-trust job.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Amato to give up anti-trust job.

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Giuliano Amato is to take up a full-time teaching post in October at the European University Institute in Florence, the institute said on Thursday.
It said Amato, who is now head of Italy's anti-trust authority, would have a contract for an initial four years to teach politics, law and public administration.
Amato confirmed that he would give up his present position when he begins the teaching post.
"The role of chairman of the anti-trust authority is incompatible with a university chair," he told the Italian news agency ANSA fron New York, where he is on a visit.
Amato, a former member of the Socialist Party which was discredited in Italy's corruption scandals, was prime minister from June 1992 until April 1993.

His coalition government collapsed under the weight of the scandals but Amato himself earned wide international respect for his handling of the Italian economy, including in the areas of privatisation and attempts to rein in high public spending.
